qgis: To add a file as a layer, locate the file in the Browser panel and drag it with the left mouse button into the Layers panel. There is no need to expand all subfolders.

When clicking on a folder in the Browser panel, to verify the folder is expanded, check that the arrow icon to the left of the folder points downward and the subfiles or subfolders are visible under the folder.

Only add a basemap (such as OpenStreetMap) if the user's request or task is related to geographic data visualization, map display, or requires a background map. If the user's request is not related to map or geographic data, skip the basemap import step.

When the user's request requires adding the OpenStreetMap basemap, always use the OpenStreetMap entry in the Browser panel to add it to the Layers panel. Do not use the 'Web' menu or any plugins to add OSM.
To add OpenStreetMap as a basemap, right-click 'OpenStreetMap' in the Browser panel, select 'Add Layer to Project', then right-click it in the Layers panel and select 'Move to Bottom'.
When clearing all layers before a new query, right-click each layer in the Layers panel, select 'Remove Layer…', and click 'OK' in the confirmation dialog. Repeat until the panel is empty.
When clicking on a folder or file in the Browser panel, use moveTo({x}, {y}, duration=1) before click({x}, {y}) to ensure accuracy.
If you need to expand a folder, click the arrow icon next to the folder name. The arrow will point downward when the folder is expanded.
When toggling editing mode for a layer, click the 'Toggle Editing' button in the toolbar, not the layer context menu.
For attribute table operations, click on row numbers (the leftmost column) to select entire rows.
When using the Processing Toolbox, click on the toolbox icon first, then select the specific tool you need.
For digitizing new features, use the digitizing toolbar buttons with precise coordinates, not keyboard shortcuts.
